responsibility: `rustc_type_ir` provides rustc’s interner-agnostic type intermediate representation: a shared, compiler-wide model of Rust’s types, regions, constants, aliases, trait objects, generators, and related forms that can be used independently of any particular compiler context. The crate root in `lib.rs` serves as the integration surface for this representation by assembling and re-exporting the crate’s pieces and by defining foundational type-system indices and enums such as De Bruijn indices, universes, bound variables, variance, and closure kinds, making the common IR utilities available to the trait solver and other compiler crates. The core semantic shape of the IR lives in `sty.rs`, which defines the main interner-parameterized enums and structs for type-system values and equips them with the standard comparison, hashing, stable hashing, formatting, and serialization hooks needed for compiler use. `codec.rs` complements that representation by defining the interner-aware encoding and decoding interfaces for type IR values, including shorthand support for repeated types and predicates and reconstruction of interned values in the destination interner. Together, these files make this crate the stable abstraction layer that represents, transports, and exposes Rust type information across rustc components.
